Introduction When using Amazon CloudFront, many users adopt a "multi-domain" architecture — associating multiple domains under a single Distribution to share configuration, including origin configuration, security configuration, CDN configuration, and network configuration. While this simplifies management, it also introduces some notable problems: 1.1 Limitations of the Multi-Domain Architecture Cache operations cannot be performed per domain: when you need to refresh the cache of a specific domain, you can only refresh the entire Distribution's cache, affecting all domains. Security policies cannot be implemented per domain: all domains share the same WAF rules, making it impossible to customize security policies for different domains. Configuration management cannot be performed per domain: origin, CDN, and network configurations are all shared, so you cannot adjust them independently for a single domain. 1.2 Using CloudFront SaaS Manager Features to Transform to a "Multi-Tenant" Architecture We will leverage CloudFront SAAS manager features to transform the existing "multi-domain" architecture into a "multi-tenant" architecture, enabling advanced application scenarios under a multi-tenant model.
